question.text:
Given below are two reactions of water with sodium and carbon dioxide. What is the nature of water in these reactions?

(i) 2Na+2H2O→2NaOH+H2

(ii) 6CO2+12H2O→C6H12O6+6H2O+6O2

options.text: In (ii) water acts as an oxidising agent and in (i) it acts as a reducing agent
In (i) water acts an an oxidising agent while in (ii) it acts as a reducing agent
In both, (i) and (ii) hydrogen acts as a reducing agent
In both, (i) and (ii) hydrogen acts as an oxidising agent

solution.text: With sodium metal water acts as an oxidising agent and gets reduced to  <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> , with  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>  water acts as a reducing agent and is oxidised to oxygen.
